judge.decision:
Build A-EUR in BOTH arms of append_version_changes, taking COMPLETE's shape with MINIMAL's cost frame. In the fold's existing per-Tender pass, carry the previous version's elected EUR value. Pass `value_moved` (NULL<->value counts as a move) into append_version_changes and add `|| value_moved` to the lot arm (lots present on both sides) and to the tender arm, beside 533's `closed_before != closed_now`. Compare EUR cents, not the published figure, because the bound compares EUR. Option 2 is rejected: it saves about a quarter of the rows, changes the return type of the election 551 deployed hours ago, and leaves crossings caused only by the exchange rate unprobed for good. B is rejected: on 2026-10-15 a value-bound lots subscriber held 119-145 lots wrongly at EUR 100k/1M, every day, and a resume never re-snapshots. That fails 493's 'negligible reach' test (493 measured 0 of 14,480). A-wide is deferred to its own issue rather than slipped in under 560.

The tender arm is in because it costs nothing and closes a real hole. All 5,512 version pairs on 10-14/10-15 already had a tender row, so it adds about 0 tender rows. It matches 533, which put closure in both arms. Without it, 547's promise that 'a Tender whose current version leaves a bound always arrives as removed' is false for a version whose facts, rounds and groups are identical while a non-EUR value moves with the rate.

No PROJECTION_EPOCH bump, no refold, no backfill. No stored column changes. The change log is append-only, and the refold and rederive paths already announce head differences (ADR-0017 D3 rule L announces every head lot when the head differs; D5 for rederive). So a refold of millions of Tenders would buy nothing here.

Cost: about 1.1k-2.8k extra lot `changed` rows per daily append. That is +12-18% on daily-shaped windows; the +59% in W2 was a fold batch, not a day. About 1M rows a year against a 955M-row log. Fold cost is one in-memory head election per written version.

Two things neither design covered, and the build must include both:
(1) /docs Live feed (crates/app/src/v1/docs.rs:496) and the OpenAPI EventStream description (crates/app/data/openapi.json:1153) list 560 as a known exception, and the docs.rs test at ~2038 asserts "(issue 560)" is there. All three change.
(2) Those same surfaces say 'the diff stream then makes your final state exact' apart from 560 and 562. But version_predicates reads country, cpv, buyer, winner, bidder, procedure_type and the deadline at the Tender version (tid, seq), not per lot. So on /v1/lots those filters miss a move whenever no lot row is written. Retiring 560 must not leave /docs claiming more than is true: the retired exception is replaced by an honest one that names a new follow-up issue.

judge.rationale:
The house rule puts correctness of served SSE events ahead of effort, with a refold only where the reach justifies one. A needs no refold, so the only question is reach against row cost.

Reach is real and recurs every day. Both independent measurements found 133-165 versions per day (MINIMAL) and 141 versions in a daily-shaped 5-hour window (COMPLETE, W1) where the elected EUR value moved while about 1,000-1,900 surviving lots got no lot row. At EUR 100k and 1M bounds, 119-145 lots a day are held wrongly, and an SSE resume never re-snapshots, so the error piles up until the client reconnects without a cursor. 493 kept its gap at 0 of 14,480; 560 fails that test by orders of magnitude.

A is the 533 mechanism applied to value. A Tender-level input that the lot is filtered on moves, so the lot gets a `changed` row. It brings the append path into line with ADR-0017 D3 rule L, which already announces every head lot when the head differs.

What the fold needs is already there. The running ScalePartners exists, set_head is a full overwrite, so the keep>0 seed is exact (pinned by the prefix test), and head_value_eur_cents_with is the same election the head column stores. That includes 551's derived lot sums, so a sibling lot moving a derived head is covered.

Compare EUR, not the published figure, because the bound compares EUR. Moves caused only by the rate are 5.5% of the extra rows in the daily-shaped window, so exactness is cheap. Option 2 would also change a struct deployed hours ago and leave a permanent caveat.

On the tender arm, MINIMAL said it is not needed, which is right on volume (0 of 5,512 pairs lacked a tender row). COMPLETE adds it, and I take COMPLETE's side: it costs nothing, matches 533's both-arms shape, and makes 547's /v1/tenders 'removed always arrives' promise true for versions with identical facts where only the rate moved.

Over-delivery to unfiltered lot consumers (+12-18% lot rows on daily-shaped windows, about 1M rows a year against 955M) is the kind D3 already accepts. SSE probe cost per extra row is the same shape every eForms lot-party version already pays.

Two gaps in both designs are fixed in the units. The /docs and OpenAPI Live-feed text and its docs.rs test pin the 560 exception, so the build must update them. Retiring that exception alone would let /docs over-promise exactness while the wider class of Tender-scope filters on /v1/lots stays open (version_predicates reads (tid, seq)). U-a files that class as its own issue with A-wide's numbers, and U-c's docs name it, so A-wide's volume decision (+36-136% lot rows, reversing 493) is made on its own evidence.

Golden snapshots digest the change log, so a deliberate, reviewed regeneration is part of U-b. In the On-mode refold, the first appended version must compare against the compared prefix's last value; U-b computes it there and test (c) pins it.

No prod reads were spent; both designs' measurements agree on the order of magnitude and the decision does not depend on the gap between them.

objections: REACH IS OVERSTATED ABOUT 5x FOR THE PERSISTENT ERROR, AND NEITHER DESIGN CREDITED SEQ-LESS ROWS. Both measurements count a lot as silent only when no lot row exists at version_seq = seq. But the daily fold converts a TED version published today at yesterday's fixing (docs/operations.md:307-311). The next morning, rederive-eur-recent re-derives it, and inplace.rs Moved::announce writes ADR-0017 D5 rule-L seq-less `lot changed` rows for every lot of a head that has a moved row. So almost every non-EUR TED head is re-announced, all of its lots, about a day later. Measured on prod (1 bounded read, 3.8 s; plan-checked; the query is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-tender-db/3050fd14-5ca6-5dd7-8b63-f827e13fd8ce/scratchpad/d56x/adv/q_adv.sql, the output in q_adv.out). For 2026-10-14 TED, 1,011 of the 1,165 me_lots got a seq-less lot `changed` on 10-15, and 1,009 of those 1,011 sit on versions with a non-EUR amount. Of the 124 EUR-only lots, 2 were covered. All 103 FTS lots are uncovered: FTS is folded the day after publication with the correct rate, so D5 never moves it, and these moves are rate-only (mp_lots is 1). The gap that persists forever is about 124 + 30 + 103 = roughly 257 of 1,268 lots a day (~20%), not 1,069-1,268. The '119-145 lots/day held wrongly and piling up' figure is mostly next-morning-corrected for TED. The decision still holds: about 250 lots a day still accumulate, far beyond 493's 0 of 14,480. But the rationale, the 560 record and the CHANGELOG rest on the wrong framing. For most TED non-EUR rows, A buys latency (next morning becomes immediate). For EUR-only and FTS Tenders it buys correctness.

A ALONE DOES NOT CLOSE THE GAP WHEN SEVERAL VERSIONS OF A TENDER ARE FOLDED IN ONE RUN. ValueBy::Version is exact only at t.current_seq. At any other version, both At probes read the superset (read.rs ~1186-1230 and 1424-1470). apply_tender_tx writes all of a Tender's appended versions in one transaction, so SSE probes every non-last appended version superset-vs-superset, every time. Under max_value on a multi-lot Tender the superset is almost always true, so such a row classifies as (true,true) `changed`. An in-to-out move (400k to 1M, then 1M) never sends `removed`, and an out-to-out move (1M to 2M, then 2M) upserts a lot that is outside the bound. The run's last version writes no lot row because its value did not move. Measured (1 bounded read, 2.0 s; d56x/adv/q_run.sql and q_run.out): on 10-14, 151 of 2,751 later TED versions were followed by another version of the same Tender published the same day. 17 TED and 9 FTS value-moving versions were followed that day by a version that did not move the value: 83 + 21 lots, about 10% of A's rows and about 40% of the persistent reach. U-c's api test and U-b's store tests fold one version at a time, so they cannot see this. The cross-run version of the same artifact (a client that resumes after its Tender has moved on) is 561's. Today /docs says that applying `changed` as an upsert makes the state right, which is false in that case.

THE U-d BAR AND ITS STOP RULE WILL MISFIRE. q3 counts silent lots by seq rows only and reads stored eur_cents after the rederive. After A, a TED non-EUR version whose previous version was published the day before is folded with that same D-1 fixing on both sides, so the fold sees no move. The next morning the rederive moves it, and D5 covers its lots with seq-less rows. q3 will report those lots as residue whose elected value DID move, which is U-d's stop condition, although nothing is wrong. Separately, the 10-16 drains (550 project 2531, 2563/2564, 551's 2573-2575) wrote millions of seq-less corrections. Any day whose D5 morning overlaps a drain makes a 'covered' count meaningless.

THE GOLDEN REVIEW RULE CANNOT BE CHECKED AS WRITTEN. fold_writer.snapshot digests the change log with rowid and cursor as its first columns (table_digest(db, "changes", "cursor", ...); rows look like `5|5|'tender'|1|3|'changed'`). One inserted row renumbers every later row of that phase, so the line diff will not be 'only inserted lot|changed / tender|changed rows'. project_golden's change digest has no cursor (kind|op|seq|entity_id), so a line diff works there. Its Off-mode refold replays the whole history, so expect more inserted rows than the append phases suggest.

OFF AND SHADOW REFOLDS AND REBUILDS GET MORE EXPENSIVE, AND THE DECISION DOES NOT SAY SO. With TENDER_REFOLD_COMPARE=off or shadow, and on a rebuild, append_version_changes runs for every version of every Tender. A then writes value-moved lot rows across all of history, on the order of W2's +59% lot rows, or O(versions x lots) on long non-EUR chains, plus one election per version everywhere. On is the default, so this does not block, but the cost and ops notes claim 'negligible' only for daily appends.

THE SEED FOR A PURE APPEND IS RECOMPUTED, NOT READ FROM WHAT SUBSCRIBERS HOLD. When keep == stored.len() and the Tender is not stale, the stored head value (StoredIdentity.head.value_eur_cents) is already read, free, by tender_identity's SELECT. It is what every snapshot and head probe saw. A recomputed of_chain(prefix) value differs from it whenever the election or the rates changed without a refold of that Tender, for example a head that 551's walk did not stamp. In that case A can skip a row that a subscriber needs. This is minor and rare.

THE RATE-ONLY SHARE IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS THE RECORD. The judge leans on COMPLETE's W1 figure of 5.5% (all native figures identical). MINIMAL's me-not-mp measure on 10-14 is about 27%: FTS 102 of 103 lots, TED 237 of 1,165. 'Exactness is cheap' holds either way, in absolute rows. But the record should not state 5.5% as the share.
amendments: U-b: ADD A NET-MOVE RULE AT THE LAST VERSION THE LOOP WRITES. Keep `run_seed` = the value before the first version written in this run: the keep>0 prefix value, or the compared prefix's last value in On mode. When i + 1 == p.versions.len() and a seed exists, set value_moved |= (value_now != run_seed), so the head itself is probed whenever the run's net value moved. Tests: (i) one fold run that appends v2 (EUR 1M to 2M) and v3 (2M) writes `lot:LOT-1@3:changed`; (ii) an api.rs variant where v2 and v3 fold in ONE batch before the subscriber reads. Starting from 400k, then 1M, then 1M under /v1/lots?max_value=50000000, it must end with `removed`. Without the rule it ends with `changed`.

U-b test (c): use a compared prefix of two or more versions with different values, for example [1M, 400k]. Assert that appending 1M writes a lot row, and that appending 400k writes none. This catches a comparison against None or against a stale earlier prefix value in both directions.

U-b: for a pure append (keep == stored.len(), !stale), also set value_moved on the first appended version when stored_identity.head.value_eur_cents != value_now. The value is already read and costs nothing. Do not hold the whole HeadValue across an await, only the Option<i64>: apply_tender_tx's future is already stack-sensitive (the goldens run on_a_big_stack). Reuse the hoisted `rates` Arc in the post-loop head UPDATE. The rates stay the same Arc, and the election logic stays separate.

U-b (d): review fold_writer.snapshot with the rowid and cursor columns stripped. Compare the kind|entity_id|seq|op sequence of each phase, and require it to differ only by inserted lot/tender `changed` rows, with matching changes= and row-count headers. The commit message records that check.

U-d: change the read. (a) Count a silent lot as covered when a seq-less lot `changed` row follows within the next morning's rederive window. Report seq-row coverage and D5 coverage separately (the q_adv.sql encoding does this in one 4 s pass). (b) Set the bar on lots that neither path covers, against the pre-deploy baseline measured the same way: about 257 lots on 2026-10-14 (TED EUR-only 122, TED non-EUR 32, FTS 103). The rough bar 'falls to <=25% of 1,069-1,268' is out of scale once D5 is credited. (c) Treat a residue version as a stop only when its value moved at FOLD-TIME rates. A move that only the next morning's rederive introduced is a D5 case, not a defect. (d) Choose a publication day whose D5 morning has no refold or drain running.

Record of 560 and the CHANGELOG (U-c): restate the reach. Before the deploy, TED heads with a non-EUR amount were already re-announced to lot streams by the next morning's rate rederive (D5). The gap that persisted was EUR-only Tenders and FTS, about 250 lots a day in measured silent lots, not 1,069-1,268. Qualify 'including moves caused only by the rate': a TED version published today is compared at yesterday's fixing, and the next morning's rederive still re-announces its lots. Keep the advice to re-subscribe once, for EUR-only Tenders and FTS.

U-c /docs and OpenAPI: do not claim that the diff stream makes the final state exact under min_value/max_value for a client that resumes or lags past a version since superseded. Both probes then read the superset, and a `changed` can name an entity outside the bound until a later change probes the current version. Name 561 for this. Record the in-run and cross-run superset artifact in 561 with the 151-of-2,751 same-day figure.

U-a: say that its starting numbers (W1 3,619 / W2 17,012 uncovered lots) include lots A now covers, and do not credit D5 or rule-L seq-less corrections. Re-baseline after U-d before A-wide's volume is weighed.

Cost note in 560: an Off-mode or Shadow epoch refold, and a rebuild, now writes value-moved lot rows for every historical version. That is on the order of W2's +59% lot rows, or O(versions x lots) on long non-EUR chains. On mode is unaffected beyond one election at the compared prefix's last version.

judge.decision:
Decision: A. Store each version's elected value and read it in the At probe, with the superset kept as a guarded fallback. Build it the way COMPLETE's A1 describes, but fill it lazily as in A2: no dedicated all-profile refold.

What gets built:
- A column on the version row, `tender_versions.value_eur_cents`. `write_version` (canonical.rs:40803) writes it using `head_value_eur_cents_with(v, partners, rates).eur_cents`, over the running `ScalePartners` that is already set for that version (canonical.rs:22849-22853). So the stored value is exactly what the head column held when that version was the head (issue 375's rule: the fold's own function, never SQL).
- A quiet compare rule. When only this column differs, the compare runs one single-column UPDATE. It does not rewrite the whole version (D1.4) and writes no rule T/L correction row (D3). It is counted as `values_refreshed`, so `verified + corrected == stamped` still holds.
- `PROJECTION_EPOCH` goes from 4 to 5.
- An epoch-gated reader in `ValueBy::Version`, in this order:
  - at the head: the head column;
  - when `t.projection_epoch >= 5`: `v.value_eur_cents`;
  - otherwise: today's superset, with `t.projection_epoch < 5` added to each of its subqueries.
  The superset code stays for good. It is the fallback for a rolled-back binary, which stamps 4, for Tenders stamped 0, and for Tenders no fold has touched yet.

How it fills: every fold that touches an epoch-4 Tender after the deploy fills all of that Tender's versions. It does so in the same transaction that writes that Tender's new change rows. So every transition row written from the deploy on is probed exactly, and that is the live traffic. The remaining Tenders fill with the next all-profile refold that runs for any other reason (ADR-0017 D6). No R4 is run for 561 alone, because the only thing left on the superset is replay of change rows written before the deploy, on Tenders not folded since.

Rejected:
- B, keeping the superset for good. It leaves about 16-19 % of max_value probes with the wrong op on live traffic, permanently.
- N and B+. They are partial fixes, and B+ risks the forbidden under-delivery direction.
- A sibling table. It needs a second 14.9 M-row B-tree and an extra seek per probe, and an older binary would leave orphan rows that break the FK.
- A dedicated R4 now. Its reach beyond the lazy fill is close to nil.

judge.rationale:
The standard here is that correctness of served SSE events comes before effort, while a refold of millions of rows has to earn its keep through reach. A splits cleanly along that line. The build fixes the live traffic. The refold would only fix history, so the decision skips the refold and keeps the build.

**Reach of the defect.** Both designers measured it independently and got the same answer.
- Live window, 2026-10-16 07:39-12:54 UTC, 3,260 tender transitions with seq >= 2:
  - max_value: 18.9 / 16.1 / 10.5 % wrong ops at EUR 100k / 1M / 10M;
  - min_value: 4.4 % at EUR 1M.
- Head proxy, 10-14, 2,376 heads: 502-597 over-reads at the typical max_value bounds.
- That is about 300-600 wrong-op events a day for one max_value subscriber, multiplied about 10x on lots streams.
- It includes an EUR-0 class the issue does not name (167 of 524 at EUR 1M), and min_value over-reads that mostly come from 551's lot-sum leg.
- The error is one-sided: 0 false negatives across 14 head×bound sets. A client following the served contract (upsert on `changed`, idempotent delete on `removed`) therefore still ends with exact state. What it loses is the event itself: `added` arrives as `changed`, which an alert-on-added client misses, and it gets spurious `removed` events.

That is a served-event correctness defect at high frequency per subscriber. Zero live streams in one /metrics sample argues for low urgency, which is why the build is sequenced after 551 and batched. It does not argue for keeping a wrong op for good.

**Only A is exact.** The election cannot be written in SQL (issues 366/375).

**Why no dedicated refold.**
- Change rows are written by the fold, inside the same transaction that compares the stale chain. With the epoch bump, every Tender that receives a change row after the deploy is filled before that row exists.
- A2's analysis holds: every post-deploy transition probe is exact without an R4.
- Correction rows probe head against head-1, and their label does not depend on the old side: if the new side is false they deliver `removed`, if true an upsert. So unfilled Tenders do not hurt them.
- What an R4 would add is exactness only for clients that resume from a cursor older than the deploy, and replay rows of Tenders untouched since. Those reads still only over-deliver.
- That is not a reach that justifies 6-7 hours of whole-corpus folding. The fill rides the next all-profile refold instead (D6).
- The epoch split is cheap. R3 checks read `= 0` (operations.md:960), the R4 window check matters only at the next R4, and the daily project pays one whole-chain compare for each epoch-4 Tender it touches, about 3-5k a day, which is seconds.

**Design choices taken from COMPLETE.**

The tests and unit 5's ~1,000-Tender canary limit a mistake to over-announcing about 1,000 Tenders.
- The epoch gate makes a rollback safe. An older binary stamps 4 and leaves the column out of its compare, so readers fall back to the superset.

objections: The accepted residual is the forbidden failure, and its window is described wrongly. Here is how it happens. A lagging subscriber reads row N of a Tender while N is no longer the head and the Tender is at epoch 4 or 0. The new side then reads the superset, which over-reads, so the subscriber gets a false added/changed. The fill then commits. When the subscriber reads row N+1, the old side at N is exact (outside), and if N+1 is outside too the result is (false,false) -> `continue` (sse.rs). The subscriber keeps a ghost Tender until that Tender enters the bound and leaves it again. Before 561 the superset was consistent across both reads, so row N+1 delivered `removed`. The window is not milliseconds. It is the time the subscriber takes to catch up from row N to row N+1, which is unbounded for a resumed cursor. Under the lazy fill it stays open for every unfilled Tender until unit 6, and unit 6's R4 fills millions of Tenders while subscribers may be catching up. It recurs on any 0->5 re-stamp that is not announced (scoped refolds). rederive-eur and resolver re-stamps are safe, because the seq-less correction rows they write later deliver `removed` through the in-place (false,false) arm. The change also makes /docs line 496 false ('the diff stream then makes your final state exact, with two known exceptions') and CHANGELOG's 'a Tender whose current version leaves a bound always arrives as removed'.

The claims of 'no extra seek' and 'O(1)' are wrong for `v`. AND seq=?)` to `sqlite_autoindex_tender_versions_2 (tender_id=?)`, which walks every version of the Tender on each probe. Today's lots At shapes seek the PK. Any non-key `v` column triggers it (v.published_at does too), so the real tenders At probe, whose SELECT list names v.published_at/publication_id/notice_subtype, very likely walks already today. judge.decision:
## Decision (2026-10-17): B. A fold that moves a Tender's label announces it with ADR-0017 D3's seq-less rows, and the read path stays as it is

**What to build.** In `Db::apply_tender_tx`, `tender_identity` already sets `StoredIdentity.moved` when it rewrites `source` or `kind` in place (canonical.rs ~23200-23216). Today only the acting compare-On stale path reads that flag (~23027). With this change, every fold that is not `acting` and has `moved` set writes D3's rows through `inplace::correction_rows`, last for the Tender:
- rule T, a seq-less tender `changed`;
- one seq-less lot `changed` for each lot of the head version.

This also covers the unchanged-chain early return. `acting` folds are left alone, because D3 already writes one set there. A rebuild never sets `moved`. No change to SQL, plans, schema or the read path. No refold, no drain.

**What subscribers see.** SSE's in-place arm (sse.rs:404-465) probes head and head−1 under the new label:
- A `source=doe` tape, or an old-kind tape, gets `removed` for the Tender and for each head lot.
- A `source=ted` tape gets `changed`.

**Verify changes.** The `source=ted` tape hears `changed`, not `added`. /docs already says to apply that as an upsert (ADR-0017 D4, and 547's decision for value bounds). The Verify's `added` is replaced by `changed`.

**Measured.** Both designs read prod, bounded, and agree:
- Visible DÖE→TED flips run at about 110-150 a week, all on Mondays and Tuesdays: 100 on 10-05, 44 on 10-06, about 58 on 10-12, 51 on 10-13. These are weekend DÖE publications whose TED twin arrives one daily cycle later.
- 147 flips with 225 head lots in the window of TED versions published 10-12 to 10-16.
- Every flip has a seq-carrying tender row at the TED version.
- Today each flip leaves a permanent ghost in a `source=doe` subscription.
- Kind moves: 0 in 12,794 later versions.
- 1,128 of the 1,275 DÖE+TED merges in that window were co-minted or minted TED-first, so `moved` stays false and B never touches them.
- B's cost is about 370 extra seq-less rows a week.

**Not built:**
- **Option 3 (announced-label columns `source_prior`/`source_since`).** It only buys exact operations: `added` instead of `changed` on the new-label tape, and no extra `removed` on unrelated filtered tapes. The house bar for the diff stream is an exact final state, with over-delivered `removed` (164/287) and `changed`-as-upsert (D4, 547/561) as the accepted errors. Clients have to keep upsert handling anyway for `max_value` (561), so op-exactness for `source` alone saves them nothing. The cost is an M-sized build: a schema change on a public, allow-listed table, and a new invariant ("the label as announced at a seq") that every replay, every stale refold under Off/Shadow/On, and every rebuild must keep. Its failure mode is the error the house does not accept. A stale `source_since` after a later prepend to a flipped Tender gives a doe tape a fake `added` at v1, unless a clamp rule holds on every path. B can never send an old-label tape anything but `removed`.
- **A (per-version source read from notices).** It reports the 1,128 co-minted and TED-first merges as DÖE at v1. That is about 226 fake added/removed pairs a day, to close a gap of about 29 a day. It also puts an EXISTS join on notices, which the CASE does not short-circuit, on every source-filtered At probe. And it cannot fix kind.
- **C (keep the gap).** About 110-150 permanent ghosts a week, roughly 2% of weekly DÖE intake. Not negligible.

**No correction walk for past flips.** A single metrics read showed 0 live SSE streams, and webhooks and polls are unfiltered. A stream that resumes across the deploy keeps its earlier ghosts until it re-snapshots, and the CHANGELOG says so.

**Reopen if** the docs ever drop "apply `changed` as an upsert". Option 3's columns are the shape to build then.

Both At probes read the single rewritten `t.source`/`t.kind` (read.rs:3029-3035, lots read.rs:3989). The old-label tape gets (false,false) and `in_place_changed`, so `removed`. The new-label tape gets (true,true), so `changed`, or (false,true), so `added`, for a lot first written at the head. The v2 transition rows still go to the old-label tape as (false,false) on a non-removed op and are dropped (`continue`). So the correction is the only event that reaches it, and it is a re-assertion of the head state, which is safe under every other filter as well. `moved` is set only in tender_identity (canonical.rs:23202), the only writer of tenders.source/kind. Acting and the D3 branch do not overlap: acting = shadow && On, shadow requires stale && !stored.is_empty(), and the early return requires !stale. I found nothing that breaks 551's derived heads: B touches no head column, and ValueBy::Version (read.rs:1424) is re-read only as the head, exact, against head−1, a superset, which is the current in-place behaviour.

An existing test will go red and the decision does not name it. In crates/ingest/tests/project.rs:1187, `a_refold_corrects_a_stored_tender_kind` part 1 sets `kind='procedure'` by hand, then stamps the Tender stale and refolds. The head-lot source in unit 2(a) has a hole. 'The lot ids the write loop resolved for p.versions.last()' is empty when the chain shrank back to its kept prefix (keep == p.versions.len() < stored.len()): the write loop never runs, and the head's VersionLots rows are on disk, not in `pending`. The realistic case is a TED notice regrouped out of a group whose last version it was, which flips ted→doe. B would then write rule T only, and a `source=ted` lots tape would keep ghosts of the head lots.

The fixture question for unit 2(b) has an answer already, and the decision leaves it open. The fold cannot move `source` on an unchanged chain: `fold` emits one version per group notice, and `primary_source` reads those same notices' sources (project.rs:3796, 6619). A STORED label that disagrees with the derivation, followed by a bare requeue, does reach the early return with moved=true. Part 2 of `a_refold_corrects_a_stored_tender_kind` (project.rs:1235-1250) already drives exactly this, and asserts (tenders_unchanged, tenders_written) = (1, 0). Those are real flips that B will also announce. So 'the 1,128 are never touched' should read 'at most 1,128', and about 370 rows a week is a floor. The new-label tape first hears `changed` with `version: 2`: the transition row is classified (true,true), because both probes read the rewritten label. The `version: null` correction then repeats it. designs.why:
Most DÖE-to-TED merges never reach a subscriber as DÖE-only. In 5 days, 1,275 Tenders gained a TED version over a DÖE v1. Only 147 (about 29 a day) were on the feed before their TED notice arrived. Option 2 reads 'source at a version' from the notices. That reports the 1,128 as DÖE at v1, so every doe stream would hear about 226 fake added/removed pairs a day to close a 29-a-day gap. It also puts a notice join, which the CASE cannot short-circuit, on every source-filtered At probe.

Option 3 keeps the label the fold actually announced: the prior label and the seq from which the new one holds. It writes them only when the label moves. So it is op-exact for the 147, leaves the 1,128 reading exactly as today, and costs about 1 forced row a day. It needs no refold or backfill and leaves the At-probe plans unchanged (checked locally). Its kind half is the same correction as option 1, because kind is constant within a chain and only moves when v1 is replaced.

Option 1 is the cheapest correct-final-state fix: about 74 rows a day, no schema change. But it can never give the ted tape `added`, because both in-place probes read the one `t.source`.
